item.title: Envision targets end-2028 completion of its Galaxy AI data centre campus in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, with eventual capacity of up to 3 GW
item.description: Ricky Zheng, general manager of Envision Group's AI data centre business, told Bloomberg TV on 30 October 2026 that the wind and battery maker plans to finish its Galaxy Campus at Ulanqab, about 350 km northwest of Beijing, by the end of 2028, with capacity eventually reaching 3 GW. Envision began operating the site in August. It provides power and supporting systems while tenants install their own chip clusters, and Zheng said offtake agreements are already lined up through 2029 or 2030. He said Envision aims for as much as 10 GW globally over the longer term. Caveat: single interview; tenants, chip mix and phasing beyond the first phase were not disclosed. Country conversion: China pairs inland renewable power with leased AI halls. [Signal 52, Single-source, via Bloomberg News (via Energy Connects), 30 Oct 2026, interview with Envision's Ricky Zheng] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: AM Intelligence reportedly seeks up to $3 billion of bonds and loans to buy Nvidia Rubin GPUs for its India and Malaysia build
item.description: Bloomberg reported on 30 October 2026, as relayed by CNBC, that Hyderabad-based AM Intelligence, owned by the founders of Greenko, plans to raise up to $3 billion through bond issues and bank loans to purchase Nvidia Rubin GPUs, and expects about $300 million in advance payments from potential offtakers. The split between bonds and loans is not final. The company said on 5 October it would invest $6 billion for 100 MW split across India and Malaysia with 29,000 Rubin chips. Caveat: report based on unnamed sources; the company did not respond to CNBC. Country conversion: India's largest Rubin order outside North America moves to debt financing. [Signal 44, Single-source, via CNBC 30 Oct 2026, citing Bloomberg] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Canada commits up to C$1.6 billion of equity in Cohere; Cohere commits at least C$1.7 billion to computing infrastructure in Canada by 2030
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced on 29 October 2026 that the Government of Canada will make an equity investment of up to about C$1.6 billion in Cohere, alongside private investors including NVIDIA, Bell and Schwarz Group. In return Cohere commits to at least C$1.7 billion of additional computing infrastructure in Canada by 2030, at least 1,000 new Canadian technical jobs by 2030, and to keep its Canadian incorporation and headquarters. The investment is staged, with regular reporting against those commitments. Caveat: no site, capacity in MW, chip count or provider for the compute was disclosed, and the total round size was not given. Country conversion: Canada ties sovereign model money to compute that must be built at home. [Signal 66, Confirmed, via Prime Minister of Canada news release, 29 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: UK Budget sets a Data Centre Covenant: 6 GW of AI data centre capacity needed by 2030, with grid capacity reserved for strategic sites that sign up
item.description: HM Treasury published the Data Centre Covenant with the Autumn Budget on 28 October 2026. The government estimates the UK needs 6 GW of AI data centre capacity by 2030 so it is not reliant almost entirely on overseas compute. Strategic data centres that want enhanced support must meet tests: credible commitments for the grid capacity they request, a Local Benefit Plan scaled to project size, a Power Usage Effectiveness of 1.3 or better with annual energy and water reporting, local jobs and apprenticeships with a contribution to British AI hardware, and secure access to compute for the NHS and public services. In return, ministers will use Planning and Infrastructure Act powers to reserve and reallocate grid capacity, allow transfer of pre-2030 connection contracts and, in narrow cases, temporary on-site generation. The Budget also adds £140 million for the Sovereign AI Unit. Caveat: which sites count as strategic and the full criteria are still to be published, and a draft National Policy Statement goes to consultation. Country conversion: the UK trades grid priority for local and security commitments. [Signal 70, Confirmed, via HM Treasury, The Data Centre Covenant, 28 Oct 2026 (primary); New Civil Engineer 29 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: L&T's Vyoma.AI breaks ground on a 52 MW liquid-cooled AI data centre at its Chennai AI Factory campus
item.description: Larsen & Toubro said on 28 October 2026 that Vyoma.AI, its AI cloud and hyperscale data centre business, held the groundbreaking for a 52 MW AI-ready data centre in Chennai with direct-to-chip liquid cooling, aimed at hyperscalers, neoclouds and AI developers. It sits on L&T's planned gigawatt-scale AI Factory campus in Chennai, which already runs AI compute clusters in an operational 30 MW facility and has 150 MVA of power infrastructure ready. Vyoma targets over 250 MW across India. Caveat: no completion date, tenant or cost disclosed. Country conversion: Chennai adds another domestic-owned AI build days after OneQode's 14 MW at AdaniConneX. [Signal 48, Confirmed, via Larsen & Toubro press release, 28 Oct 2026 (primary); The Hindu] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Seychelles Cabinet approves a sovereign government cloud on two in-country datacentres and a 2026 to 2031 Digital and AI Strategy
item.description: State House said Cabinet, chaired by Vice-President Sebastien Pillay on 28 October 2026, approved the Seychelles Digital and AI Strategy 2026 to 2031 and the Government Cloud and Datacenter Project: a sovereign, in-country government cloud on two geographically separated datacentres, meant to reduce reliance on commercial and overseas infrastructure and provide local cloud and AI computing. Phase 1 builds the cloud and primary datacentre; Phase 2 adds the secondary site and expands cloud and AI capability. Caveat: no budget, capacity, vendor or timeline disclosed. Country conversion: a small island state moves government workloads onshore. [Signal 30, Confirmed, via State House Seychelles, Cabinet Business 28 Oct 2026 (primary); Seychelles News Agency] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: OneQode signs 14 MW of AI capacity with AdaniConneX in Chennai, in talks for up to 114 MW in India
item.description: Singapore-based OneQode said on 27 October 2026 (US Eastern; 28 October in India) it signed an agreement with AdaniConneX for 14 MW of data centre capacity at Siruseri SIPCOT, Chennai, its first major AI deployment in India, for training, inference, enterprise and sovereign workloads. The companies are discussing additional capacity of up to 114 MW, which OneQode says could generate over $6 billion of GPU-as-a-service total contract value. The build uses AMD Instinct GPUs under a May 2026 collaboration, with AMD Helios racks planned. It follows CoreWeave's 240 MW plan at AdaniConneX Navi Mumbai earlier this month. Caveat: only the 14 MW is signed; the 114 MW and $6 billion figures are company targets. Country conversion: a second foreign GPU cloud takes Indian colocation for regional inference. [Signal 52, Confirmed, via OneQode press release via PR Newswire, 27 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Brazil's 5G auction fund approves a R$375 million sovereign AI data centre for the federal government, run by Telebras
item.description: Gaispi, the group that directs projects funded by Brazil's 5G spectrum auction through the entity EAF, approved on 27 October 2026 a sovereign data centre for federal government AI projects at an estimated R$375 million, according to IA News citing Teletime and Convergência Digital. The AI module would have 20 racks, six GPU servers with 48 GPUs in total, nine CPU servers and liquid cooling, plus a separate colocation module of up to ten racks. The facility would be federally owned and operated by Telebras, with deployment estimated at 12 months depending on power, licensing and equipment delivery. Caveat: still needs approval from Anatel's board; GPU model not disclosed. Country conversion: Brazil funds a small first sovereign AI cluster from money already collected. [Signal 34, Single-source, via IA News 29 Oct 2026, citing Teletime and Convergência Digital] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Naver signs up to $9 billion Brookfield compute deal, clearing Nvidia's $1 billion equity investment; 55 MW in 1H 2027, 200 MW by 2028
item.description: Naver said on 27 October 2026 it signed a contract with Brookfield to secure up to $9 billion of AI computing infrastructure. Brookfield will fund a special purpose vehicle, Asset Co., 100% to buy GPUs and data centre capacity; it will be consolidated as a Naver subsidiary under K-IFRS. Naver Cloud operates the capacity and pays usage fees linked to business revenue instead of buying the hardware, and Naver guarantees those payments for up to 8 years. The deal satisfies the condition Naver set for Nvidia's planned $1 billion strategic equity investment (about 1.5 trillion won), which now moves to a third-party paid-in capital increase. The AI Factory hub is the Gak Sejong data centre, with 55 MW in the first half of 2027, 200 MW by 2028 and a long-term 1 GW global goal. Caveat: capital increase terms not yet announced. Country conversion: Korea's largest platform company gets financed sovereign-scale GPU capacity without putting it on its own capex line. [Signal 72, Corroborated, via Digital Today 27 Oct 2026, quoting Naver statement] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: CoreWeave brings most of 22.5 MW online at atNorth DEN01 in Copenhagen and extends its network backbone to seven Middle East and Asia Pacific markets
item.description: CoreWeave said on 27 October 2026 it has brought the majority of a planned 22.5 MW of IT capacity online at atNorth's DEN01 in Copenhagen, its first Denmark deployment, running NVIDIA Blackwell systems on Quantum-X800 InfiniBand, with surplus heat going to district heating. Its European footprint is now nine data centres in five geographies including the UK, Spain, Sweden and Norway. It is also adding network points of presence in the UAE, India, Indonesia, Singapore, Australia, Korea and Japan from late Q4 2026, closing a four-continent loop by mid-2027. Caveat: points of presence are network, not GPU capacity. Country conversion: Denmark gets live neocloud GPU capacity days after its grid priority order on data centres. [Signal 55, Confirmed, via CoreWeave IR release, 27 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Korea will trim AI data centre power demand in its 12th power plan to confirmed projects only, two months after lifting the forecast to 11.9 GW
item.description: Climate, Energy and Environment Minister Kim Sung-hwan told a National Assembly audit on 26 October 2026 that only confirmed AI data centre demand will go into the 12th Basic Plan for Long-term Electricity Supply and Demand, saying that once the three mega-projects began, 'not much demand has actually been firmed up in concrete terms'. In August the ministry had raised projected 2040 AIDC peak demand to 11.9 GW from 4 GW against an 18.4 GW by 2035 build plan (SK, GS and Naver 8.4 GW by 2029). GS has started a 1.2 GW first phase in Donghae for 2028; SK has not detailed its 4 GW of regional sites beyond the 100 MW Ulsan build with AWS. AI-DC Korea counts 522 projects (3.4 GW) in grid impact review as of Q1, of which 10 (1 GW) have secured power. The science ministry said on 27 October the mega-projects remain on track. Caveat: no reduction figure set; plan goes to the Assembly in late December or early January. Country conversion: Korea's grid planner is discounting announced gigawatts to what has firm demand. [Signal 64, Corroborated, via Seoul Economic Daily 27 Oct 2026 (minister at parliamentary audit); MSIT explanatory note 27 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Freedom Holding advances Kazakhstan's $2 billion Sovereign AI Hub: 100 MW site, first public GPU cloud in 2027
item.description: Freedom Holding said on 26 October 2026 it is advancing a $2 billion Sovereign AI Hub under a November 2025 agreement with Kazakhstan's Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development, on a site with 100 MW of available power, with Freedom as principal financing partner and operator. Its first GPU cluster will open as a public cloud in 2027, and the first phase of a Freedom AI Super Cluster is planned for Q1 2027; a Freedom Cloud data centre is under construction near Almaty. CEO Timur Turlov says demand is twice first-stage capacity and prospective clients will lease for five years. Caveat: GPU count, vendor and exact site not disclosed. Country conversion: Kazakhstan adds a domestic, financed sovereign GPU cloud alongside the Firebird export-licensed build. [Signal 50, Confirmed, via Freedom Holding Corp. press release, 26 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Anthropic's public S-1 puts numbers on its US compute rent: up to $120.5 billion with SpaceXAI, $125.2 billion Broadcom TPU lease, $44.6 billion Nscale, $41.3 billion Lambda
item.description: Anthropic filed its S-1 publicly on 26 October 2026. The filing says it agreed to spend up to $120.5 billion with SpaceXAI for NVIDIA GPU compute over terms into 2029, about $3.1 billion a month once all capacity is delivered (expected December 2026), cancellable on 90 days' notice after initial non-cancelable periods ending January and March 2027. A five-year Broadcom equipment lease for AI accelerators carries about $125.2 billion of rent excluding interest and is non-cancelable except on default; Anthropic may issue up to $42.0 billion of convertible notes to Broadcom to finance it. Nscale agreements total up to about $44.6 billion into 2033 and Lambda agreements about $41.3 billion into 2034; both accrue fees only on delivery, Nscale must use best efforts to obtain financing, and about $34.9 billion of the Lambda total can be terminated if Lambda does not secure the facility lease. First-half 2026 revenue was $16.3 billion and operating loss $693 million. Caveat: the filing leaves the total commitment figure blank; third-party totals (Yahoo Finance about $430 billion non-cancelable) are estimates. Country conversion: the largest single disclosed book of rented compute, mostly sited in the US, now has public terms. [Signal 70, Confirmed, via Anthropic S-1, SEC EDGAR, 26 Oct 2026 (primary); Yahoo Finance 26 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Meta launches a $95 billion equity financing plan for AI infrastructure: $35 billion underwritten now, $60 billion at-the-market from Q1 2027
item.description: Meta announced concurrent underwritten offerings of about $22.5 billion of Class A common stock (via forward sale agreements) and about $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred depositary shares, plus a planned $60 billion at-the-market program in non-voting Class C stock that is not expected to start before Q1 2027. NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom indicated non-binding interest in buying up to $5.0 billion of the Class A shares. Meta reiterated 2026 capex of $135 to $145 billion, said it owns data centers in 23 US states, is building four superclusters of more than 1 GW each and is on track to nearly double infrastructure capacity in 2026. It generated $97 billion of operating cash flow in the first three quarters and held about $82 billion of cash and securities. Caveat: the ATM program has no signed agreement and its timing, size and terms are not set. Country conversion: a US hyperscaler is now funding its compute build with new equity, not only cash flow and debt. [Signal 66, Confirmed, via Meta investor release 26 Oct 2026 (primary); CNBC 26 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Anwar says SoftBank's Son plans $50 billion of AI and data centre investment in Malaysia, with sites in Kuching, Sarawak and the peninsula
item.description: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on 24 October 2026 that SoftBank Group chairman Masayoshi Son had identified locations in Kuching, Sarawak and peninsular Malaysia for planned investments of $50 billion in AI, new technologies and data centres, after a video call earlier that week (Bloomberg via CNBC). Sarawak Premier Abang Johari confirmed on 26 October that the plan includes an AI data centre at Tanjung Embang. Earlier in October SoftBank signed a framework with Grab and Petroleum Sarawak Berhad to explore AI and digital infrastructure in Sarawak. Malaysia recorded RM385.7 billion ($94 billion) of data centre related investment from 2021 to 1H 2026 (MIDA). Caveat: SoftBank had not commented; no MW, timeline or binding agreement disclosed. Country conversion: Malaysia's pipeline moves beyond Johor toward Sarawak hydropower. [Signal 62, Corroborated, via CNBC citing Bloomberg, 26 Oct 2026; Malay Mail and The Star, 26 Oct 2026 (Sarawak Premier)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: SpaceX signs binding commitment for an Apollo-managed master finance lease covering about $40 billion of GPU pods
item.description: SpaceX's 8-K (filed 26 October 2026) says that on 24 October it entered a binding commitment letter for a master finance lease under which an Apollo-managed entity will buy and lease GPU pods and related equipment for data centers SpaceX selects. Tranches carry lease terms of about five to five and a quarter years, rent is quarterly in advance at one-twentieth of financed cost plus a fixed rate set at pricing, and aggregate principal payments are expected to total about $40 billion. Closing is expected before year end, with lease schedules starting in the first half of 2027 as GPUs arrive. Elon Musk posted that the deal had closed and that debt markets have almost entirely shut for companies without substantial non-data-center revenue. Caveat: the filing describes a commitment subject to closing conditions, not a closed financing, and does not name the GPU model or sites. Country conversion: US GPU capacity financed against an investment-grade, non-AI revenue base. [Signal 60, Confirmed, via SpaceX 8-K, SEC EDGAR, 26 Oct 2026 (primary); CNBC 25 and 26 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: UK Treasury previews Budget AI package: extra £60 million for the Sovereign AI Fund and £18 million for an Advanced Chip Design Academy
item.description: HM Treasury said on 24 October 2026 that the Chancellor will make AI part of next week's Budget, including an additional £60 million for the Sovereign AI Fund to invest directly in UK AI companies (adding Physical and Industrial AI), a further £60 million for Sovereign AI's R&D Procurement Scheme, £18 million for a new UK Advanced Chip Design Academy, AI chip design capability in Edinburgh, an AI Centre of Excellence in Manchester and £10 million a year to study AI's effect on jobs. Caveat: these are announced allocations ahead of the Budget, not compute capacity, and no data center, power or GPU figures were given. Country conversion: small sovereign capital, aimed at chip design and firms rather than megawatts, a week after Microsoft left Nscale's Loughton site over grid delays. [Signal 38, Confirmed, via GOV.UK (HM Treasury) 24 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: SK Hyper seeks about $350 billion for the first 5 GW of a 15 GW South Korean AI data center plan by 2035
item.description: SK Hyper CEO Chung Suk-keun told Bloomberg TV on 23 October 2026 that the SK Telecom unit is in talks with big tech companies and financial investors to fund 15 GW of data center capacity in South Korea by 2035, and that the first 5 GW phase alone would need about $350 billion (about 463 trillion won) including servers and equipment. It targets a first outside round by end 2026 or early 2027, plans phased operations from 2029, and starts with a 900 MW Ulsan project alongside a 100 MW AWS facility, aiming for a 2 GW plus Yeongnam cluster and further GW sites in Chungcheong and the southwest. Chung put Korea's current data center market at about 1 GW and said the plan depends on drawing inference and training demand from Japan, Taiwan and other Asian markets. SK Telecom plans to invest up to 750 billion won in SK Hyper through 2030. Caveat: an estimate for a financing-dependent plan; no investor, term sheet or customer has been named, and the pace will follow demand. [Signal 58, Corroborated, via Bloomberg TV 23 Oct 2026; Seoul Economic Daily 23 Oct 2026; Business Times 23 Oct 2026; Hankyung 23 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Kazakhstan signs Firebird investment agreement as Firebird secures a US export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs
item.description: During Jensen Huang's first visit to Astana on 23 October 2026, Firebird signed an investment agreement with the government of Kazakhstan at the Akorda presidential palace. NVIDIA says Firebird has secured a US export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs; the first phase is under construction with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley in Ekibastuz, targeting commercial launch in Q3 2027, and a planned second phase would take Firebird's potential capacity in Kazakhstan to about 500 MW. Kazakhtelecom has already deployed 400 H200 and 480 B300 GPUs in Astana and Almaty and plans more than 1,000 GPUs at Data Center Valley plus more than 1,000 Vera Rubin GPUs in the Ekibastuz region in 2027. NVIDIA also announced an investment in Kazakhstan-founded Higgsfield AI. Huang called the country a future 'AI factory hub for all of Europe' (CNBC). Caveat: no contract value, power source or financing was disclosed, and the second phase is planned, not committed. Country conversion: a named US export license turns Kazakhstan's Ekibastuz plan into licensed GPU supply. [Signal 62, Confirmed, via NVIDIA blog 22 Oct 2026 (primary); Astana Times 23 Oct 2026; CNBC 23 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: G42's Khazna and Core42 sign MoUs with Copelouzos to explore an AI factory in Greece
item.description: Copelouzos Group said it signed memoranda of understanding in Athens on 22 October 2026 with G42 portfolio companies Khazna Data Centers, which would lead the physical build, and Core42, which would provide cloud and AI compute for banking, telecoms, shipping and public administration, during a UAE Ministry of Foreign Trade business mission. Copelouzos is also developing GREGY, a 3,000 MW Egypt-Greece power interconnector. Caveat: exploratory; scope, site, capacity, financing and timelines are to be defined, subject to definitive agreements and approvals. Country conversion: Greece gets its first Gulf-operator AI factory proposal, tied to an energy group. [Signal 38, Confirmed, via Copelouzos Group press release via Zawya, 22 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Crusoe and Araico plan an AI cloud site at Paraguay's Itaipú substation: initial capacity mid-2027, path to 106 MW, options to about 280 MW
item.description: Crusoe announced on 22 October 2026 a partnership with Paraguayan developer Araico to build AI compute next to the Itaipú substation, powered by the Itaipú hydroelectric dam. An initial deployment is planned for mid-2027 with a path to 106 MW of IT capacity and long-term options to about 280 MW. Araico leads site development; Crusoe operates the compute for Crusoe Cloud, serving US and Latin American customers. It is Crusoe's first AI cloud deployment in Latin America. President Santiago Peña backed it, and US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, present at signing, said it could be the largest private foreign investment in Paraguay's history. Caveat: no capex figure or GPU count disclosed. Country conversion: Paraguay's surplus Itaipú hydro gets its first named neocloud tenant. [Signal 70, Confirmed, via Crusoe newsroom and GlobeNewswire, 22 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Texas environmental regulator suspends at least 17 data center construction stormwater and wastewater authorizations and shuts its online permit portal
item.description: After Public Citizen and FracTracker reported that automated approvals kept flowing despite Governor Greg Abbott's pause on data center permits, the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality suspended at least 17 stormwater and wastewater authorizations tied to data center projects and closed its online application system; applications must now be filed physically. TCEQ says all data-center-related notices of intent are suspended and that these automated notices do not authorize operation, though they are required before clearing land of an acre or more. The governor's office says no state agency will approve data center permits until the PUC, ERCOT and the Water Development Board have the information they need. Caveat: the count of 17 comes from the watchdog groups; TCEQ and the governor's office dispute that any permit was improperly approved. Country conversion: the largest US build state has paused the paperwork that starts construction. [Signal 52, Corroborated, via Houston Public Media 22 Oct 2026; Texas Tribune 21 Oct 2026; Tom's Hardware] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Humain and NVIDIA plan up to 84 MW and about 27,000 GPUs in Saudi Arabia, including 50 MW of Vera Rubin for an unnamed US client
item.description: At NVIDIA GTC Berlin on 22 October 2026, Humain (PIF-owned) and NVIDIA announced an expanded collaboration covering a multi-phase rollout of up to 84 MW of AI compute in Saudi Arabia, about 27,000 GPUs. Phase one is 14 MW of NVIDIA Blackwell HGX B300 systems, about 6,000 GPUs on Quantum-X800 InfiniBand, with deployment starting in Q4 2026 for Humain Cloud customers. Humain then expects 70 MW of Vera Rubin infrastructure, about 21,000 GPUs, from June 2027: 50 MW for frontier-scale workloads of an unnamed US-based client and 20 MW for Humain Cloud from July or August 2027, all on the NVIDIA DSX platform. The National reports the Vera Rubin phases remain subject to final agreements. Humain targets nearly 3 GW of data center capacity by 2030 and more than 6 GW by 2034. Caveat: no primary release URL was found at our cutoff; figures are from The National and Data Centre Magazine, which quote both companies. Country conversion: a second named offtake for Saudi export compute in two days, after Nebius at Oxagon. [Signal 64, Corroborated, via The National 22 Oct 2026; Data Centre Magazine 22 Oct 2026 (company quotes)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Google and Voltus expand to a 1 GW Google-funded virtual power plant across PJM
item.description: On 22 October 2026 Google and Voltus announced an expanded agreement to build a 1 GW virtual power plant across the PJM region (13 states plus Washington, D.C., about 67 million people). Voltus aggregates flexible demand from businesses and homes, such as smart thermostats, batteries and industrial assets, that cut use during peaks; Google funds it and participants receive bill savings and cash payments. It is a tenfold expansion of a 100 MW agreement from earlier in 2026, and Google calls it one of the largest distributed capacity portfolios deployed by a hyperscaler. The release gives no cost, timeline or link to specific Google campuses. Country conversion: in the tightest US capacity market, a hyperscaler is buying demand response at gigawatt scale to make room for its own load. [Signal 62, Confirmed, via Google blog 22 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: UK industry taskforce with NVIDIA, Microsoft and Cisco tells ministers they have about 12 months to win local consent for data centres
item.description: The Guardian reported on 22 October 2026 (exclusive) that the Sovereign AI Leadership (SAIL) taskforce, whose members include NVIDIA, Microsoft and Cisco, told the UK government it has a window of roughly 12 months to build a compact that earns public consent before US-style organised opposition takes hold. The submission asks for a national framework of recommended local-benefit terms for councils and mayors, including an indicative contribution scaled to site size, and for host councils to keep more business rates. It cites dry summers and rising energy bills as drivers of scrutiny. Action to Protect Rural Scotland says 15 community campaigns are already active in Scotland. A government spokesperson pointed to existing measures letting councils in England's AI growth zones keep all additional business rates. Caveat: single outlet; the submission itself was not published. Country conversion: the industry is asking Britain to pay for social licence before the build-out, after Microsoft's Loughton exit and NextDC's consent-driven delay. [Signal 58, Single-source, via The Guardian 22 Oct 2026 (exclusive)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Bull and CRA sign MoU for the Czech AI Gigafactory bid, first deal under the France-Czech AI pact
item.description: Bull and Ceske Radiokomunikace (CRA) said on 21 October 2026 they signed a strategic memorandum to combine CRA's infrastructure with Bull's systems, software and services in the CRA-led consortium bidding for the Czech AI Gigafactory (AIGF CZ) under the EU AI Gigafactories programme. It is the first industrial agreement under the bilateral AI and digital cooperation agreement signed by French minister Anne Le Henanff and Czech minister Karel Havlicek. Bull says its Czech and French manufacturing with Foxconn could build the servers, and it plans to reserve capacity for its own clients. CRA runs eight data centres and already sells GPU capacity. Caveat: non-binding; capacity, site, chips and cost not disclosed, and the EU selection is pending. Country conversion: Czechia positions a telco-led bid as the Central and Eastern European gigafactory candidate. [Signal 46, Confirmed, via Bull press release, 21 Oct 2026 (primary); CRA press release] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Crusoe takes Polar's 40 MW DRA02 building at Tørdal, Norway, for Vera Rubin NVL72; DRA01 live at 12 MW
item.description: Polar Data Centers said on 21 October 2026 that DRA01 at its hydro-powered Tørdal campus in Norway is live with 12 MW of IT capacity running Crusoe Cloud, and that Crusoe will take DRA02, a second liquid-cooled building of 40 MW critical IT expected live in late 2027, where Crusoe plans to deploy Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72. Caveat: GPU count and contract value not disclosed. Country conversion: Norway's hydro campuses keep converting into US neocloud capacity, now on the Rubin generation. [Signal 50, Confirmed, via Crusoe / Polar press release, 21 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Oman signs Yamna to build a large AI data centre in Salalah; first phase over £1 billion
item.description: The UK government said on 21 October 2026, during Sultan Haitham bin Tarik's state visit, that UK-founded Yamna would sign an agreement with Oman to build a large-scale AI data centre in Salalah, with a first phase expected to exceed £1 billion. Yamna said it signed a strategic cooperation agreement with Oman's Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology for the project, branded Salalah Al Khadra Digital. UK Export Finance raised its capacity for UK exports to Oman to up to £7 billion. Caveat: MoU stage; MW, power source, tenant and chips not disclosed. Country conversion: Oman enters the Gulf AI campus race with a southern site away from the Gulf states' existing hubs. [Signal 44, Corroborated, via GOV.UK (FCDO) 21 Oct 2026 (primary); Yamna statement] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: IREN secures grid power and a civil works license for a planned 300 MW AI campus in Badajoz, Spain, targeting 2028
item.description: At NVIDIA GTC Berlin on 21 October 2026, IREN announced it has secured grid-connected power and the civil works license for a planned AI data center of about 300 MW in Badajoz, Extremadura, with initial operations targeted for 2028. The campus uses closed-loop liquid cooling, is designed for NVIDIA DSX compatibility, and will offer managed AI cloud services for customers with data residency requirements. IREN also set up IREN Europe, chaired by former Banco Santander CEO Angel Corcostegui, with Roberto Purcaro as Executive Director for Europe. IREN entered Spain in June 2026 by buying developer Nostrum Group. Europa Press reports construction should start between late 2026 and early 2027. No customer, capex or GPU count was disclosed. Country conversion: Spain gets a permitted, grid-connected 300 MW neocloud site while UK projects stall on grid queues. [Signal 54, Confirmed, via IREN release 21 Oct 2026 (primary); Europa Press 21 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: South Korea's chip exports hit a record US$27.5 billion for 1 to 20 October, up 222.5%, 44.7% of all exports
item.description: Preliminary Korea Customs Service data released on 21 October 2026 show South Korea's total exports for 1 to 20 October at US$61.6 billion, up 105.4% year on year and a record for the period. Semiconductor exports rose 222.5% to US$27.5 billion and made up 44.7% of total exports, up 16.2 percentage points from a year earlier; computer peripherals rose 424.0%. Imports rose 42.8% to US$47.1 billion. The data are preliminary. Working-day-adjusted daily exports rose 65.9%, so part of the headline jump reflects more working days than in the same period of 2025. Country conversion: memory and AI server pricing is now the main driver of Korea's trade account, days before SK hynix (28 Oct) and Samsung (29 Oct) report. [Signal 56, Confirmed, via Korea Customs Service via Korea.kr briefing 21 Oct 2026 (primary); Yonhap 21 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html
